page0.text:
Speaking of which, I haven't seen Rider all day.
Knowing her, she's keeping watch over Sakura from the shadows nearby. I should say hi to her if she's around.

page1.text:
Rider's nowhere to be found in the house.
She has her own bedroom, but there's no sign she's ever used it.
I try to think of a location she likes that would also give her a vantage point of Sakura's room,

page2.text:
and decide it has to be here.
The only place she can hide with no one else around, while watching Sakura from a distance, is the shed.

page3.text:
"Are you in here, Rider?"
I call out into the empty shed.
"I am standing by. What do you need, Shirou?"
Rider appears along with her aura. She must have been in spirit form.

page4.text:
"..."
Now, then.
I just came to say hello, but now that we're face to face, I'm getting nervous.
Rider tends to keep people at a distance...and that doesn't particularly bother me, but as a healthy young man, I'm not sure where to point my eyes when I'm around her.

page5.text:
"...I asked you if you had business with me."
"Oh, uh, I'm not really here for that. I haven't greeted you today, so I just thought I'd come say good morning."

page6.text:
"...I see. You must be very idle."
She replies bluntly.
But I expected this much. It's actually easier for me that she's this way.

page7.text:
"Yeah, I'm free. I'm just wandering around since I have nothing to do. Is this where you stand guard over Sakura?"
"Yes. I am her Servant.
I will not protect you or Rin Tohsaka unless she orders me to."

page8.text:
"Really? Good, that makes me feel better."
I sigh in relief.
I was worried that Sakura might be pushing herself too hard.

page9.text:
"Thanks, Rider. Keep taking care of Sakura."
I wave and leave the shed.
"...Wait. I have a question."
"Hm?"
I stop before I return to the yard.

page10.text:
"What? There isn't a lot I can tell you."
"It is a question about you, so I'm sure you can answer.
Shirou Emiya. I do not understand your behavior.
Why are you relieved that I refuse to protect you?"

page11.text:
"Huh? Is that all?
Sure, having you be my bodyguard would bring some peace of mind, but I think a man should protect himself.
As for Tohsaka...well, whatever happens, I'm sure she'll figure things out."
"...You think you can protect yourself, with that body? That just sounds like bluffing to me."

page12.text:
"It is a bluff. I'm weak in a fight, so bluffing's all I have.
...If I'm being honest, I'm pretty nervous. But I want you to stay the way you are. If you move, that'll exhaust Sakura, and I don't want her to use any more magical energy."

page13.text:
"I see. It is true that Sakura would suffer if I were to act.
Even taking material form places a burden on her, so you don't want to increase my workload unnecessarily."

page14.text:
"That's right. I want you to only protect Sakura.
Though, I might ask you to look after Illya too, if I kick the bucket."
"How self-serving. You would ask me for help in your most trying time, even though you know I'm an obstacle?"

page15.text:
"Well, yeah...is that bad?"
...
Rider doesn't answer.
She's staring straight at me through her blindfold.

page16.text: "Ah, then I'll make you a deal. If you're ever in a pinch, I promise to help you. Will you help Illya then? It's give and take."

page17.text: "I cannot answer that. It's likely that if I were ever in dire straits, you would already be dead. Your proposal is not very tempting."

page18.text: "Gah. Yeah, I guess it wouldn't matter much if I was dead by the time you're in trouble. Sorry, that was pretty self-serving of me."

page19.text:
...I'm in a bind, then.
In that case, it would be best if I took Illya to a safer location.
She doesn't want to go to the church, and I'd rather not leave her alone in her castle...

page20.text:
"...Honestly, you are so unreliable."
"Huh? Did you say something, Rider?"
"Yes. I will consider your offer. If you save me from a desperate situation, then I promise to honor your wishes. Is that acceptable, Shirou?"

page21.text:
"Oh... R-really!? But you said I was being selfish!"
"We can serve our mutual interests. But only if you help me, first."

page22.text:
...
My eyes widen.
...I'm happy that Rider took me up on my offer, but more than that...

page23.text:
"Rider, did you just laugh?"
"No. There was nothing to be happy about, so there's no reason I would have smiled."
"But I saw you laugh, good reason or not. It was a really subtle change, so I almost missed it."

page24.text:
"That's impossible. I'm saying it didn't happen, so you must have misunderstood."
Rider flatly denies it.
Hmm. If she's that insistent, maybe I really was imagining it.

page25.text:
"..."
"..."
Mrgh. This is an awkward silence.
I was planning to just go back to the house, but there's something about the way Rider is looking at me that seems to pull me in.
She's as cool and stoic as ever, but I feel like she wants to say something else.

page26.text:
"..."
"..."
The tension in the air feels nearly confrontational.

page27.text:
Also...
This thought just came out of nowhere, but Rider's tall.
Her hair is long, and her legs are slender and well-proportioned.
I've only ever seen her face once, but she was incredibly beautiful under her mask.
Tohsaka and Sakura are beautiful too, but Rider's on a different scale entirely.

page28.text:
"Do you have a question, Shirou?"
"Huh? It's no big deal, but can I ask you something?"
"I do not mind. What is it?"
"Okay. You're pretty tall, Rider. How tall, exactly?"
I ask her frankly.

page29.text:
...Wait.
Why is she backing away from me?

page30.text:
"Rider?"
"N-no, there's no reason for this. Think nothing of it."
"...Okay. So how tall are you? If you're taller than me, you have to be more than 170 centimeters."
"I...I cannot answer your question. Please ask me something else."

page31.text:
"You can't answer...? You don't know how tall you are?"
"That's not what I meant... Ask me something else, Shirou. If you repeat that again, it will upset me."

page32.text:
"Mrgh."
I'm clearly making her uncomfortable.
If she's this anxious, then maybe...

page33.text:
"Rider, are you insecure about your height?"
...
Rider stiffens.
I appear to have hit the nail on the head.

page34.text:
"..."
"..."
We both fall silent again.
Then, when it becomes too much for Rider to bear...

page35.text:
"I-is that so strange of me?"
"Huh? It isn't strange. I just wasn't sure why you froze up. Why do you care so much about your height?"

page36.text:
"...I think the reason is evident enough. Surely, you must feel the same way. A tall woman like me is ugly and not lovely at—"
"Why not? I think you look cool, Rider."
Talk about a trivial insecurity.
I sure wish I could be that tall.

page37.text:
"..."
"..."
Another silence.
I'm starting to wonder if I'm interfering with Rider's guard duty.

page38.text:
"Um. Am I bothering you, Rider?"
"Well, I was hiding to be on guard against any attack by Zouken. If you come speak to me, then it defeats the purpose of concealing myself."
"Right. I should be getting back. Sorry for bothering you."
"Ah... W-wait, Shirou."

page39.text:
For the second time, I stop and turn around.
Rider hesitates and bites her lip.

page40.text:
"...If you are free at the moment, then please look in on Sakura. Her mood changes greatly when you're not around."
"Oh...okay, I'll go right now. She does tend to push herself as soon as I take my eyes off her. I'll make sure she's resting."

page41.text:
Rider's right.
The guesthouse is just over there, so I should go look after Sakura.

page42.text:
"Oh, right. I forgot the reason I came out here to begin with."
I turn back to Rider for the third time.

page43.text:
"W-what, Shirou?"
"Good morning, Rider. I hadn't actually said it yet."
Good, good.
I'm so dumb for forgetting what I came here to say.

page44.text:
And then...
"...Good morning, Shirou. Allow me to make a remark as well."
Rider goes back to her usual attitude, watching me.

page45.text:
"Hm? What?"
"You waste time on trivial matters. It is too late to say 'good morning.' We are in the afternoon now."

page46.text:
"Oof, that's embarrassing. To be honest, I forgot about you until just earlier."
"It seems so. Take greater care in the future.
Also, please disregard what I said earlier."
"Huh? What do you mean?"
"About how you must think me a nuisance. Allow me to amend that statement."

page47.text:
"I don't think you're a nuisance at all, Rider."
"Yes, I know that now. After all, you came here solely to greet me, and for no other purpose."

page48.text:
Turns out I didn't imagine it.
Now that I'm face to face with Rider, I can see that she's wearing a happy smile.
